about:
Sentec, the Swiss-American medical device company that acquired Percussionaire Corporation in February 2024, operates a manufacturing facility in Sandpoint, Idaho. Founded in 1999, Sentec began as a deep-tech venture focused on respiratory care, developing noninvasive monitoring and therapeutic technologies for patients across acute and chronic care settings.

The company designs, develops, and manufactures its product lines entirely in-house, including transcutaneous monitoring (TCM) systems that continuously measure blood gas parameters, the LuMon™ system which uses electrical impedance tomography (EIT) to visualize regional lung function at the bedside, and the IPV®1 intrapulmonary percussive ventilation device. With over 300 employees globally, Sentec maintains manufacturing sites in Sandpoint and Therwil, Switzerland, alongside operational offices in Lincoln, Rhode Island; Landquart, Switzerland; Budapest; Bad Soden, Germany; and Australia.

Sentec sells directly to hospitals and clinical institutions worldwide, serving neonatal intensive care units, pediatric and adult critical care, and respiratory therapy departments. Its noninvasive solutions aim to reduce the need for invasive blood draws and support ventilation management for complex respiratory patients.

Sentec emphasizes a flat organizational structure and interdisciplinary collaboration as cultural differentiators, arguing that this model accelerates innovation in noninvasive respiratory technology. The company states its mission is to enable less invasive care through accurate, safe, and easy-to-use monitoring and therapeutic devices.
